page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical AMD EPYC 9B14 cores with 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranking in the top 25% and Geekbench text processing also scoring in the top 25%. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations show clear performance limitations. The stress-ng multi-core performance, Geekbench multi-core score, and Passmark memory score fall into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show weak throughput, with uncached read operations at 37.53 GB/sec and write operations at 15.4 GB/sec.

This instance is configured for workloads that benefit from single-threaded execution and dedicated CPU allocation but do not require large memory footprints or high memory bandwidth. Suitable workloads include single-threaded text processing, basic web serving, and lightweight single-threaded compression tasks. It is less suitable for memory-intensive database operations, multi-threaded software compilation, or medium-to-large language model inference due to the low memory capacity and weak multi-core scaling. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a low-cost entry point to dedicated AMD EPYC hardware for compute-bound tasks that fit within its 8 GB memory limit.

The instance provides 2 physical cores with hyper-threading, but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile: single-core CPU performance and text processing are strong, placing in the top 25%, whereas multi-core scaling and memory bandwidth are weak, with the Passmark memory score falling in the bottom 10%. This resource density makes the instance qualitatively cost-effective for single-threaded compute tasks that fit within a strict 8.0 GB memory envelope. It is suited for lightweight text processing, single-threaded compression, and basic web serving, but is constrained for memory-heavy databases or multi-threaded compilation.
